options.c: the effect of inflation on real wages
options.d: the one-for-one relation between GDP and unemployment

questions.text: Why does expected price level P^e enter wage bargaining?

options.a: Because nominal wages are set after the actual price level is known with certainty.
options.b: Because P^e is the unemployment rate.
options.c: Workers and firms care about the expected real wage/purchasing power rather than only the nominal wage.
options.d: Because expected prices determine the money multiplier.

questions.text: An increase in expected prices P^e, other things equal, tends to:

options.d: leave nominal wages unchanged by definition

questions.text: A higher unemployment rate tends to reduce negotiated wages because:

options.a: unions become more aggressive as job loss becomes irrelevant

options.d: the real wage on the PS curve rises

questions.text: The variable z collects structural factors that:

options.c: are identical to the markup θ

questions.text: Which change would be represented as an increase in z in the course?

questions.text: Which is another example of a higher z?

options.d: the expected negotiated real wage W/P^e negatively to unemployment u

options.a: to the right with no wage effect
